rows.evidence: Q1: Abstract and Materials and methods - the authors ran the HidroMORE model (FAO56 ET with Sentinel-2 NDVI) over the olive area of M<U+00E9>denine 2016-2019 and compared outputs with their own gravimetric soil water content measurements at four orchards. Q2: Validation results, Table 2 - simulated soil water content compared with measured values (overall R2 0.72, IA 0.76); Simulation results, Figures 5-8 - spatial maps of depletion and stress coefficient show mountain/piedmont zones least stressed (water harvesting structures) and inner plain most affected, and that by 2019 all zones fell under severe stress; Conclusions - authors state the study offers an objective tool to prioritise orchards for intervention during extended drought. Q4: Model description and Figure 7 - the model computes the intermediate variables (soil water depletion, stress coefficient Ks, adjusted ET) and these are checked against measured soil water content. Q5: Table 2 and Figure 8 - results reported separately for four agro-ecological zones (coast/Zarzis, inner plain/Dar Dhaoui, piedmont/Ksar Jedid, mountains/Zammour) with distinct soils and climates. Q6: Model simulation section - simulation performed for the entire olive land-use area of the governorate (about 200,000 ha, 8588 km2 governorate). Q7: Discussion (model evaluation and simulation) and Conclusions - authors state from their results that a finer, accurate soil map with correct soil characteristics is crucial for the simulation to guide decision-making, and that the correct soil inputs explained the better performance in Zammour and Ksar Djedid. Q8: Discussion - persistent overestimation of soil water content, coarse 1/200,000 soil map with misidentified soils, underestimated root-depth variability within zones, weather-station density causing mis-represented rainfall in 2019, FAO56 ET underestimation; Methods - no soil moisture data for 2018 and irregular sampling frequency.
rows.notes: Q2 answered yes with reservation: the study's own result is a validated spatial drought-stress map; the 'prioritizing interventions' use is the authors' stated application of that map, not a tested intervention outcome. The passage's statements on water harvesting and soil type come from model output patterns, not from a controlled test. Q3 no: ground soil moisture data served only to validate the model; the stress distribution itself rests on one method (model). Q9 no: Table 2 gives RMSE and a standard deviation of soil water content values per zone, but no dispersion or propagated uncertainty for the drought-stress estimates themselves; p-values only.

notes: Full text available including figures captions and Table 2; equations are not rendered in the text but do not affect the ratings.
